children.name: Madoqua
children.description: Madoqua — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Madoqua guentheri
children.description: Günther's dik-dik is a small antelope found in arid zones of East Africa.

children.name: Madoqua kirkii
children.description: Kirk's dik-dik is a species of small dik-dik antelope native to Eastern and Southern Africa. It is believed to have six subspecies and possibly a seventh existing in southwest Africa. Dik-diks are herbivores, typically of a fawn color that aids in camouflaging themselves in savannah habitats.

children.name: Madoqua phillipsi
children.description: Salt's dik-dik is a small antelope found in semidesert, bushland, and thickets in the Horn of Africa, but marginally also in northern Kenya and eastern Sudan. It is named after Henry Salt, who was the first European to acknowledge the species in Abyssinia in the early 19th century.

children.name: Madoqua piacentinii
children.description: The silver dik-dik is a small antelope found in low, dense thickets along the southeastern coast of Somalia and in Acacia-Commiphora bushland in the Shebelle Valley in southeastern Ethiopia. It is the smallest species of dik-dik, with a length of 45–50 cm (18–20 in), a height of 30–33 cm (12–13 in), and a weight of 2–3 kg (4.4–6.6 lb). Its back and flanks are grizzled silvery, while the limbs, ears, and muzzle are ochraceus in colour.

children.name: Madoqua saltiana
children.description: Salt's dik-dik is a small antelope found in semidesert, bushland, and thickets in the Horn of Africa, but marginally also in northern Kenya and eastern Sudan. It is named after Henry Salt, who was the first European to acknowledge the species in Abyssinia in the early 19th century.

children.name: Ammotragus
children.description: Ammotragus — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Ammotragus lervia
children.description: The Barbary sheep, also known as aoudad, is a species of caprine native to rocky mountains in North Africa and parts of West Africa. While this is the only species in genus Ammotragus, six subspecies have been described. Although it is rare in its native North Africa, it has been introduced to North America, southern Europe, and elsewhere.

children.name: Pseudois
children.description: Pseudois — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Pseudois nayaur
children.description: The bharal (Pseudois nayaur), also called the blue sheep, is a caprine native to the high Himalayas..

children.name: Pseudois schaeferi
children.description: The bharal (Pseudois nayaur), also called the blue sheep, is a caprine native to the high Himalayas..

children.name: Naemorhedus
children.description: Naemorhedus — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Naemorhedus baileyi
children.description: The red goral is a species of even-toed ungulate in the subfamily Caprinae in the family Bovidae. It is found in India, China (Tibet) and Myanmar. Its natural habitats are seasonal mountainous areas 1,000 to 2,000 meters above sea level.

children.name: Naemorhedus caudatus
children.description: The long-tailed goral or Amur goral is a species of ungulate of the family Bovidae found in the mountains of eastern and northern Asia, including Russia, China, and Korea. A population of this species exists in the Korean Demilitarized Zone, near the tracks of the Donghae Bukbu Line. The species is classified as endangered in South Korea, with an estimated population less than 250.

children.name: Naemorhedus goral
children.description: The Himalayan goral (Naemorhedus goral) or gray goral is a bovid species native to the Himalayas.

children.name: Naemorhedus griseus
children.description: The Chinese goral, also known as the grey long-tailed goral or central Chinese goral, is a species of goral, a small goat-like ungulate, native to mountainous regions of Myanmar, China, India, Thailand, Vietnam, and possibly Laos. In some parts of its range, it is overhunted. The International Union for Conservation of Nature has listed it as a "vulnerable species".

children.name: Bos
children.description: Bos — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Bos acutifrons
children.description: Bos acutifrons is the most ancient representative of the genus Bos cattle.

children.name: Bos bubalus
children.description: Bubalus is a genus of Asiatic bovines that was proposed by Charles Hamilton Smith in 1827..

children.name: Bos frontalis
children.description: The gayal (Bos frontalis), also known as mithun or Drung ox, is a large semi-domesticated cattle in the Himalayan foothills of Indian Subcontinent and primarily in Northeast India..

children.name: Bos grunniens
children.description: The yak, also known as the Tartary ox, grunting ox, hairy cattle, sarlak or sarlyk, or domestic yak, is a species of long-haired domesticated cattle found throughout the Himalayan region, the Tibetan Plateau, Tajikistan, the Pamir Mountains, and as far north as Mongolia and Siberia. It is descended from the wild yak.

children.name: Bos javanicus
children.description: The banteng (Bos javanicus; ), also known as the tembadau, is a species of wild bovine found in Southeast Asia, with domestic-wild hybrids present in parts of Northern Australia..

children.name: Bos planifrons
children.description: Bos acutifrons is the most ancient representative of the genus Bos cattle.

children.name: Bos priscus
children.description: The steppe bison (Bison priscus, also less commonly known as the steppe wisent and the primeval bison) is an extinct species of bison which lived from the Middle Pleistocene to the Holocene.

children.name: Bos sauveli
children.description: The kouprey (Bos sauveli), also known as the forest ox and grey ox, is a possibly extinct species of forest-dwelling wild bovine native to Southeast Asia..

children.name: Bos taurus
children.description: Cattle are large, domesticated, bovid ungulates widely kept as livestock. They are prominent modern members of the subfamily Bovinae and the most widespread species of the genus Bos. Mature female cattle are called cows, immature females are called heifers, mature intact males are called bulls, castrated males are called steers or oxen, and young animals of either sex are called calves.

children.name: Hippotragus
children.description: Hippotragus — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Hippotragus equinus
children.description: The roan antelope (Hippotragus equinus) is a large, savanna-dwelling antelope found in Western, Southern, and parts of Central and Eastern Africa.

children.name: Hippotragus gigas
children.description: Hippotragus gigas is an extinct species of antelope known from the Plio-Pleistocene of Africa.

children.name: Hippotragus leucophaeus
children.description: The bluebuck (Afrikaans: bloubok ) or blue antelope (Hippotragus leucophaeus) is an extinct species of antelope that lived in South Africa until around 1800..

children.name: Hippotragus niger
children.description: The sable antelope (Hippotragus niger) is a large antelope which inhabits wooded savanna in East and Southern Africa, from the south of Kenya to South Africa, with a separated population in Angola.

children.name: Syncerus
children.description: Syncerus — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Syncerus acoelotus
children.description: Syncerus acoelotus is an extinct species of bovid closely related to the Cape buffalo.

children.name: Syncerus caffer
children.description: The African buffalo is a large species of true buffalo native to Sub-Saharan Africa, where it is found in a number of disconnected ranges stretching from south-eastern Senegal through West and Central Africa to South Africa. The adult African buffalo's horns are its characteristic feature: they have fused bases that form a continuous bone shield, referred to as a "boss", across the top of the head. The African buffalo is more closely related to Asian buffalo (Bubalus) species than it is to other bovids such as American bison or domestic cattle.

children.name: Redunca
children.description: Redunca — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Redunca arundinum
children.description: The southern reedbuck, rietbok or common reedbuck (Redunca arundinum) is a diurnal antelope typically found in southern Africa.

children.name: Redunca fulvorufula
children.description: The mountain reedbuck (Redunca fulvorufula) is an antelope found in mountainous areas of much of sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Redunca redunca
children.description: The bohor reedbuck is an antelope native to central Africa. The animal is placed under the genus Redunca and in the family Bovidae. It was first described by German zoologist and botanist Peter Simon Pallas in 1767.

children.name: Damaliscus
children.description: Damaliscus — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Damaliscus korrigum
children.description: Damaliscus lunatus jimela is a subspecies of topi, and is usually just called a topi..

children.name: Damaliscus lunatus
children.description: Damaliscus lunatus is a large African antelope of the genus Damaliscus and subfamily Alcelaphinae in the family Bovidae, with a number of recognised geographic subspecies.

children.name: Damaliscus pygargus
children.description: The bontebok (Damaliscus pygargus) is an antelope found in South Africa, Lesotho and Namibia..

children.name: Damaliscus superstes
children.description: The Bangweulu tsessebe (Damaliscus lunatus superstes) is a population and possible taxon of Damaliscus lunatus (topi or sassaby), which are large African antelopes of the grasslands.

children.name: Oreotragus
children.description: Oreotragus — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Oreotragus oreotragus
children.description: The klipspringer (; Oreotragus oreotragus) is a small antelope found in eastern and southern Africa..

children.name: Budorcas
children.description: Budorcas — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Budorcas churcheri
children.description: Budorcas churcheri is an extinct species of takin that lived in the Pliocene of Ethiopia.

children.name: Budorcas taxicolor
children.description: The takin (Budorcas taxicolor);  is a large species of ungulate of the subfamily Caprinae found in the eastern Himalayas..

children.name: Capra
children.description: Capra — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Capra caucasica
children.description: The West Caucasian tur (Capra caucasica) is a mountain-dwelling goat-antelope native to the western half of the Caucasus Mountains range, in Georgia and European Russia..

children.name: Capra falconeri
children.description: The markhor (Capra falconeri)  is a large wild Capra species native to the mountain regions at the crossroads of Central and South Asia, including the Karakoram and Himalayas..

children.name: Capra hircus
children.description: The goat or domestic goat (Capra hircus) is a species of goat-antelope that is mostly kept as livestock..

children.name: Capra ibex
children.description: The Alpine ibex (Capra ibex), also known as the steinbock, is a European species of goat which lives in the Alps.

children.name: Capra nubiana
children.description: The Nubian ibex (Capra nubiana) is a desert-dwelling species of goat (genus Capra) found in mountainous areas of northern and northeast Africa, and the Middle East.

children.name: Capra pyrenaica
children.description: The Iberian ibex (Capra pyrenaica), also known as the Spanish ibex, Spanish wild goat and Iberian wild goat, is a species of ibex endemic to the Iberian Peninsula.

children.name: Capra sibirica
children.description: The Siberian ibex (Capra sibirica), also known using regionalized names including Altai ibex, Asian ibex, Central Asian ibex, Gobi ibex, Himalayan ibex, Mongolian ibex, and Tian Shan ibex, is a polytypic species of ibex, a wild relative of goats and sheep.

children.name: Capra walie
children.description: The Walia ibex (Capra walie, Amharic: ዋልያ wālyā) is a vulnerable species of ibex.

children.name: Antidorcas
children.description: Antidorcas — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Antidorcas marsupialis
children.description: The springbok or springbuck (Antidorcas marsupialis) is an antelope found mainly in south and southwest Africa.

children.name: Antilope

children.name: Antilope cervicapra
children.description: The blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra), also known as the Indian antelope, is a medium-sized antelope native to India and Nepal..

children.name: Saiga

children.name: Saiga borealis
children.description: The saiga antelope (Saiga tatarica, ) or saiga is a species of antelope which during antiquity inhabited a vast area of the Eurasian steppe, spanning the foothills of the Carpathian Mountains in the northwest and Caucasus in the southwest into Mongolia in the northeast and Dzungaria in the southeast.

children.name: Saiga tatarica
children.description: The saiga antelope (Saiga tatarica, ) or saiga is a species of antelope which during antiquity inhabited a vast area of the Eurasian steppe, spanning the foothills of the Carpathian Mountains in the northwest and Caucasus in the southwest into Mongolia in the northeast and Dzungaria in the southeast.

children.name: Neotragus
children.description: Neotragus — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Neotragus batesi
children.description: Bates's pygmy antelope (Nesotragus batesi), also known as the dwarf antelope, pygmy antelope or Bates' dwarf antelope, is a very small antelope living in the moist forest and brush of Central and West Africa..

children.name: Neotragus moschatus
children.description: The suni (Nesotragus moschatus) is a small antelope of the family Bovidae, and one of the smallest ungulates on earth..

children.name: Neotragus pygmaeus
children.description: The royal antelope (Neotragus pygmaeus) is a West African antelope recognized as the world's smallest.

children.name: Litocranius
children.description: Litocranius — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Litocranius walleri
children.description: The gerenuk (Litocranius walleri), also known as the giraffe gazelle, is a long-necked, medium-sized antelope found in parts of East Africa..

children.name: Addax
children.description: Addax — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Addax nasomaculatus
children.description: The addax (Addax nasomaculatus), also known as the white antelope and the screwhorn antelope, is an antelope native to the Sahara..

children.name: Pantholops

children.name: Pantholops hodgsonii
children.description: The Tibetan antelope or chiru (Pantholops hodgsonii) ( , pronounced ; ) is a medium-sized bovid native to the northeastern Tibetan Plateau.

children.name: Connochaetes

children.name: Connochaetes gnou
children.description: The black wildebeest or white-tailed gnu (Connochaetes gnou) is one of the two closely related wildebeest species.

children.name: Connochaetes taurinus
children.description: The blue wildebeest (Connochaetes taurinus), also called the common wildebeest, white-bearded gnu or brindled gnu, is a large antelope and one of the two species of wildebeest.

children.name: Ovibos
children.description: Ovibos — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Ovibos moschatus
children.description: The muskox (Ovibos moschatus) is a hoofed mammal of the family Bovidae..

children.name: Ovis
children.description: Ovis — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Ovis ammon
children.description: The argali (Ovis ammon), also known as the mountain sheep, is a wild sheep native to the highlands of western East Asia, the Himalayas, Tibet, and the Altai Mountains..

children.name: Ovis aries
children.description: Sheep (pl.: sheep) or domestic sheep  (Ovis aries) are a domesticated ruminant mammal typically kept as livestock..

children.name: Ovis canadensis
children.description: The bighorn sheep (Ovis canadensis) or bighorn is a species of sheep native to North America.

children.name: Ovis dalli
children.description: Dall sheep or thinhorn sheep (Ovis dalli), is a species of wild sheep native to northwestern North America.

children.name: Ovis gmelini
children.description: The mouflon (Ovis gmelini) or moufflon is a wild sheep native to Cyprus, two separate parts of Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Iran..

children.name: Ovis isphahanica
children.description: The mouflon (Ovis gmelini) or moufflon is a wild sheep native to Cyprus, two separate parts of Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Iran..

children.name: Ovis nivicola
children.description: The snow sheep (Ovis nivicola), or Siberian bighorn sheep, is a species of sheep from the mountainous areas in the northeast of Siberia.

children.name: Ammodorcas

children.name: Ammodorcas clarkei
children.description: The dibatag (Ammodorcas clarkei),  or Clarke's gazelle, is a medium-sized slender antelope native to Ethiopia and Somalia..

children.name: Boselaphus
children.description: Boselaphus — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Boselaphus tragocamelus
children.description: The nilgai (Boselaphus tragocamelus) (, literally meaning "blue cow") is the largest antelope in Asia..

children.name: Ourebia
children.description: Ourebia — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Ourebia ourebi
children.description: The oribi (; Ourebia ourebi) is a small antelope found in eastern, southern and western Africa..

children.name: Raphicerus
children.description: Raphicerus — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Raphicerus campestris
children.description: The steenbok  (Raphicerus campestris) is a common small antelope of southern and eastern Africa..

children.name: Raphicerus melanotis
children.description: The Cape or southern grysbok (Raphicerus melanotis) is a small antelope that is endemic to the Western Cape region of South Africa between Albany and the Cederberg mountains.

children.name: Raphicerus paralius
children.description: Raphicerus paralius is an extinct species of bovid belonging to the genus Raphicerus that lived in the Pliocene epoch.

children.name: Raphicerus sharpei
children.description: Sharpe's or northern grysbok (Raphicerus sharpei) is a small, shy, solitary antelope that is found from tropical to south-eastern Africa..

children.name: Aepyceros

children.name: Aepyceros melampus
children.description: The impala or rooibok (Aepyceros melampus, lit..

children.description: The Mongolian gazelle (Procapra gutturosa), or dzeren (), is a medium-sized antelope native to the semiarid Central Asian steppes of Mongolia, southern Siberia and northern China.

children.name: Procapra picticaudata
children.description: The goa (Procapra picticaudata), also known as the Tibetan gazelle, is a species of antelope that inhabits the Tibetan Plateau..

children.name: Procapra przewalskii
children.description: Przewalski's gazelle (Procapra przewalskii) is a member of the family Bovidae, and in the wild, is found only in China..

children.name: Oreamnos
children.description: Oreamnos — a genus of cattle & buffalo in the family Bovidae.

children.name: Oreamnos americanus
children.description: The mountain goat (Oreamnos americanus), also known as the Rocky Mountain goat, is a cloven-footed mammal that is endemic to the remote and rugged mountainous areas of western North America.

children.name: Oreamnos harringtoni
children.description: Harrington's mountain goat (Oreamnos harringtoni) was a species of caprine that resided in the Southwest of North America during the Pleistocene epoch..

children.name: Cephalophus

children.name: Cephalophus adersi
children.description: Aders's duiker (Cephalophus adersi), also known as nunga in Swahili, kunga marara in Kipokomo and harake in Giriama, is a small, forest-dwelling duiker found only in Zanzibar and Kenya..

children.name: Cephalophus brookei
children.description: Brooke's duiker (Cephalophus brookei) is a species of antelope..

children.name: Cephalophus callipygus
children.description: Peters' duiker (Cephalophus callipygus) is a small antelope found in Gabon, Equatorial Guinea, southern Cameroon, and northern Republic of the Congo..

children.name: Cephalophus dorsalis
children.description: The bay duiker (Cephalophus dorsalis), also known as the black-striped duiker and the black-backed duiker, is a forest-dwelling duiker native to western and southern Africa.

children.name: Cephalophus jentinki
children.description: Jentink's duiker (Cephalophus jentinki), also known as gidi-gidi in Krio and kaikulowulei in Mende, is a forest-dwelling duiker found in the southern parts of Liberia, southwestern Côte d'Ivoire, and scattered enclaves in Sierra Leone..

children.name: Cephalophus leucogaster
children.description: The white-bellied duiker (Cephalophus leucogaster) is a duiker found in central Africa..

children.name: Cephalophus natalensis
children.description: The red forest duiker, Natal duiker, or Natal red duiker (Cephalophus natalensis) is a small antelope found in central to southern Africa..

children.name: Cephalophus niger
children.description: The black duiker (Cephalophus niger), also known as in Dyula, is a forest-dwelling duiker found in the southern parts of Sierra Leone, Liberia, Côte d'Ivoire, Ghana, Benin, and Nigeria.

children.name: Cephalophus nigrifrons
children.description: The black-fronted duiker (Cephalophus nigrifrons) is a small antelope found in central and west-central Africa..

children.name: Cephalophus ogilbyi
children.description: Ogilby's duiker (Cephalophus ogilbyi) is a small antelope found in Sierra Leone, Liberia, Ghana, southeastern Nigeria, Bioko Island and possibly Gabon..

children.name: Cephalophus rufilatus
children.description: The red-flanked duiker (Cephalophus rufilatus) is a species of small antelope found in western and central Africa in countries as far apart as Senegal and Sudan..

children.name: Cephalophus silvicultor
children.description: The yellow-backed duiker (Cephalophus silvicultor) is a shy, forest-dwelling antelope of the order Artiodactyla, from the family Bovidae..

children.name: Cephalophus spadix
children.description: Abbott's duiker (Cephalophus spadix), also known as minde in Swahili, is a large, forest-dwelling duiker (small antelope) found only in a few scattered enclaves in Tanzania..

children.name: Cephalophus weynsi
children.description: Weyns's duiker (Cephalophus weynsi) is a tiny antelope found in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda, Central African Republic and western Kenya..

children.name: Cephalophus zebra

children.name: Bison

children.name: Bison alticornis
children.description: Bearing a large bony frill, three horns on the skull, and a large, four-legged body, exhibiting convergent evolution with rhinoceroses, Triceratops is one of the most recognizable of all dinosaurs and the best-known ceratopsian.

children.name: Bison antiquus
children.description: Bison antiquus is an extinct species of bison that lived in North America during the Late Pleistocene and the beginning of the Holocene from over 60,000 years ago until around 10,000 years ago.

children.name: Bison bison
children.description: The American bison (Bison bison; : bison), commonly known as the American buffalo, or simply buffalo (not to be confused with true buffalo), is a species of bison that is endemic to North America.

children.name: Bison bonasus
children.description: The European bison (: bison) (Bison bonasus) or the European wood bison, also known as the wisent ( or ), the zubr (), or sometimes colloquially as the European buffalo, is a European species of bison.

children.name: Bison schoetensacki
children.description: Bison schoetensacki, commonly as the Pleistocene woodland bison or Pleistocene wood bison, was a species of bison that lived from the Early Pleistocene to at least the early Middle Pleistocene from western Europe to southern Siberia.

children.name: Bos latifrons
children.description: Bison latifrons, also known as the giant bison or long-horned bison, is an extinct species of bison that lived in North America during the Late Pleistocene epoch ranging from southern Canada to Mexico.

children.name: Sylvicapra

children.name: Sylvicapra grimmia
children.description: The common duiker (Sylvicapra grimmia), also known as the gray duiker or bush duiker, is a small antelope and the only member of the genus Sylvicapra.

children.name: Dorcatragus

children.name: Dorcatragus megalotis
children.description: The beira (Dorcatragus megalotis) is a small antelope that inhabits arid regions of the Horn of Africa..

children.name: Tetracerus

children.name: Tetracerus quadricornis
children.description: The four-horned antelope (Tetracerus quadricornis), also called chousingha, is a small bovid antelope native to central, South and Western India, along with a smaller population in Nepal..

children.name: Capricornis

children.name: Capricornis crispus
children.description: The (Capricornis crispus) (羚羊) is a Japanese goat-antelope, an even-toed ungulate.

children.name: Capricornis milneedwardsii

children.name: Capricornis rubidus

children.name: Capricornis sumatraensis
children.description: The mainland serow is a species of serow native to the Himalayas, Southeast Asia and China.

children.name: Capricornis swinhoei
children.description: The Taiwanese serow also known as the Formosan serow, is a small species of bovid that is endemic to Taiwan.

children.name: Capricornis thar
children.description: The Himalayan serow, also known as the thar, is a subspecies of the mainland serow native to the Himalayas. It was previously considered its own species, as Capricornis thar. It is the official state animal of the Indian state of Mizoram.

children.name: Eudorcas

children.name: Eudorcas rufifrons
children.description: The red-fronted gazelle (Eudorcas rufifrons) is widely but unevenly distributed gazelle across the middle of Africa from Senegal to northeastern Ethiopia..

children.name: Eudorcas rufina
children.description: The red gazelle (Eudorcas rufina) is an extinct species or subspecies of gazelle.

children.name: Eudorcas thomsonii

children.name: Gazella dorcas

children.name: Gazella erlangeri
children.description: The Arabian gazelle (Gazella arabica) is a species of gazelle from the Arabian Peninsula.

children.name: Gazella gazella
children.description: The mountain gazelle, also called the true gazelle or the Palestine mountain gazelle, is a species of gazelle that is widely but unevenly distributed.

children.name: Gazella leptoceros
children.description: The rhim gazelle or rhim (from Arabic غزال الريم) (Gazella leptoceros), also known as the slender-horned gazelle, African sand gazelle or Loder's gazelle, is a pale-coated gazelle with long slender horns and well adapted to desert life.

children.name: Gazella marica
children.description: The Arabian sand gazelle or reem is a species of gazelle native to the Arabian and Syrian Deserts.

children.name: Gazella praegaudryi
children.description: Gazella praegaudryi was a small species of prehistoric gazelle described from late Miocene sediments near Bou Hanifia, Algeria.

children.name: Gazella psolea
children.description: Gazella psolea is an unusual prehistoric species of gazelle that lived in Africa and Arabia; it is only known from fossils.

children.name: Gazella saudiya
children.description: The Saudi gazelle (Gazella saudiya) is an extinct species of gazelle that was once native to the Arabian Peninsula.

children.name: Gazella spekei
children.description: Speke's gazelle (Gazella spekei) is the smallest of the gazelle species..

children.name: Gazella subgutturosa
children.description: The goitered gazelle (Gazella subgutturosa) or black-tailed gazelle is a gazelle native to Turkey, Georgia, Azerbaijan, Iran, parts of Iraq and Pakistan, Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kazakhstan and in northwestern China and Mongolia.

children.name: Gazella tingitana

children.name: Kobus

children.name: Kobus anselli
children.description: The Upemba lechwe (Kobus leche anselli) is a subspecies of red lechwe antelope found only in the Upemba wetlands in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

children.name: Kobus ellipsiprymnus
children.description: The waterbuck is a large antelope found widely in sub-Saharan Africa. It is in the genus Kobus of the family Bovidae. It was first described by Irish naturalist William Ogilby in 1833.

children.name: Kobus kob
children.description: The kob is an antelope found across Central Africa and parts of West Africa and East Africa. Together with the closely related reedbucks, waterbucks, lechwe, Nile lechwe, and puku, it forms the Reduncinae tribe. Found along the northern savanna, it is often seen in Murchison Falls and Queen Elizabeth National Park, Uganda; Garamba and Virunga National Park, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as well as grassy floodplains of South Sudan.

children.name: Kobus leche
children.description: The lechwe, red lechwe, or southern lechwe is an antelope found in wetlands of south-central Africa.

children.name: Kobus megaceros
children.description: The Nile lechwe or Mrs Gray's lechwe is an endangered species of antelope found in swamps and grasslands in South Sudan and Ethiopia.

children.name: Kobus vardonii
children.description: The puku is a medium-sized antelope found in wet grasslands in southern Democratic Republic of Congo, Namibia, Tanzania, Zambia and more concentrated in the Okavango Delta in Botswana. Nearly one-third of all puku are found in protected areas, zoos, and national parks due to their diminishing habitat.

children.name: Oryx beisa
children.description: The East African oryx (Oryx beisa), also known as the beisa, is a species of medium-sized antelope from East Africa..

children.name: Oryx dammah
children.description: thumb|in [[Bou-Hedma National Park, Tunisia]] thumb|Osteological specimen of a scimitar oryx in the Natural Science Research Laboratory's (NSRL) collection at the [[Museum of Texas Tech University.]] The scimitar oryx (Oryx dammah), also known as the scimitar-horned oryx and the Sahara oryx, is an Oryx species that was once widespread across North Africa and parts of West and Central Africa.

children.name: Oryx gazella
children.description: The gemsbok (Oryx gazella), or South African oryx, is a large antelope in the genus Oryx..

children.name: Oryx leucoryx
children.description: The Arabian oryx or white oryx (Oryx leucoryx) is a medium-sized antelope with a distinct shoulder bump, long, straight horns, and a tufted tail.

children.name: Taurotragus

children.name: Taurotragus derbianus

children.name: Taurotragus oryx

children.name: Rupicapra pyrenaica
children.description: The Pyrenean chamois (Rupicapra pyrenaica) is a goat-antelope that lives in the Pyrenees and Cantabrian Mountains of Spain, France and Andorra, and the Apennine Mountains of central Italy.

children.name: Rupicapra rupicapra
children.description: The chamois (; French: [ʃamwa] ; Rupicapra rupicapra), or Alpine chamois, is a species of goat-antelope native to mountainous parts of Europe and Western Asia, from the Pyrenees and the Cantabrian Mountain Range, the Alps, the Apennines, the Dinarides, the Tatra to the Carpathian Mountains, the Balkan Mountains, the Rila–Rhodope massif, Pindus, the northeastern mountains of Turkey, and the Caucasus..

children.name: Hemitragus hylocrius
children.description: The Nilgiri tahr (Nilgiritragus hylocrius) is an ungulate that is endemic to the Nilgiri Hills and the southern portion of the Western Ghats in the Indian states of Tamil Nadu and Kerala.

children.name: Hemitragus jayakari
children.description: The Arabian tahr (Arabitragus jayakari) is a species of tahr native to eastern Arabia.

children.name: Hemitragus jemlahicus
children.description: The Himalayan tahr is a large even-toed ungulate native to the Himalayas in southern Tibet, northern India, western Bhutan and Nepal. It is listed as Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List, as the population is declining due to hunting and habitat loss.

children.description: thumb|juvenile thumb|young male The mountain nyala (Amharic: የደጋ አጋዘን) (Tragelaphus buxtoni) or balbok, is a large antelope found in high altitude woodlands in a small part of central Ethiopia.

children.name: Tragelaphus derbianus

children.name: Tragelaphus imberbis

children.name: Tragelaphus scriptus
children.description: The harnessed bushbuck or northern bushbuck, is a medium-sized antelope, widespread in sub-Saharan-Africa. The harnessed bushbuck species has been separated from the Cape bushbuck, a southern and eastern species.

children.name: Tragelaphus spekii
children.description: The sitatunga (Tragelaphus spekii) or marshbuck is a swamp-dwelling medium-sized antelope found throughout central Africa, centering on the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Republic of the Congo, Cameroon, parts of Southern Sudan, Equatorial Guinea, Burundi, Ghana, Botswana, Rwanda, Zambia, Gabon, the Central African Republic, Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya..
